children: The following are significant news stories, press reports and events on Monday. ALL TIMES GMT (Poland: GMT + 2 hours):
On Monday, the Statistical Office will release preliminary data on inflation in Poland for August. Analysts polled by Reuters expect it to have increased to 3.1% year-on-year from 3.0% in July.
Data on the rate of growth of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in the second quarter will also be released. The preliminary reading indicated a 3.8% increase.

Poland expects its general government deficit to remain unchanged at 7.1% of GDP in 2027, the same level now planned for this year, fuelled by record deliveries of military equipment, Finance Minister Andrzej Domanski said on Friday.

Polish government expects dividends from state-controlled companies to rise next year compared to almost 8 billion zlotys ($2.14 billion) planned in the 2026 budget, the State Assets Minister said on Friday.

Poland's budget's planned revenue from dividends from state-controlled companies in 2027 will amount to 13.9 billion zlotys  ($3.71 billion), a 76% increase compared to 2026 planned revenues, PAP news agency reported.
On Monday, the Ministry of Finance will publish the debt supply for September.
